zh-TW.long_thesis_markdown:
## 經濟數據偏弱，Warsh談話仍推升短端殖利率

Warsh表示通膨改善不足、金融條件難稱緊縮後，美債短端大幅下跌。他沒有承諾9月升息，投資人卻提高了對這項決策的預期。2年期殖利率跳升14個基點至4.34%，為兩個多月來最大漲幅；5年期升10個基點至4.48%，10年期升6個基點至4.73%，30年期升3個基點至5.22%。

曲線這次轉為趨平，並未重演Warsh 7月記者會後的長端領跌。2s10s收窄8個基點至39，2s30s收窄11個基點至88。10年期實質殖利率上升8個基點至2.42%，損益兩平通膨率反而下跌2個基點至2.31%。美元上漲0.52%、黃金下跌2.85%，也伴隨市場提高對實質利率路徑的預期。

主席談話壓過同日上午偏弱的經濟資料。芝加哥PMI落入收縮，就業基準修正初值不是市場預期的上調而是下修，密西根消費者信心仍低於7月。這些訊號讓9月決策保持開放，但市場從Warsh對2%目標的承諾中，聽到了更迫切的緊縮理由。

半導體指數下跌3.48%，Nasdaq 100跌0.71%，S&P 500跌0.27%，VIX卻小降至14.42，整體債券ETF也僅小幅下跌。長債曾在談話期間上漲，最終仍收低；30年期殖利率比一個月前高13個基點。曲線趨平反映市場預期央行會更積極回應通膨，不代表供給與融資壓力消失。日本短債標售疲弱、新一輪AI借款，仍各自顯示資金需求持續。

## 通膨目標明確，9月決策卻未承諾

Warsh強調2%的PCE目標堅定不變，夏季數據改善尚未讓底層通膨趨勢出現有意義的進展，降溫必須清楚且夠快。他一方面質疑整體金融條件是否具有限制性，另一方面明確指出短期利率是聯準會的主要工具。即使沒有具體前瞻指引，市場仍聽出透過傳統利率政策緊縮的理由更強。

聯邦資金期貨最初將9月升息機率從談話前約36%推升至50%以上，稍後交換市場定價達約60%。巴克萊改為預測9月及12月各升25個基點，但並非所有人都跟進。ABN AMRO與Brandywine的投資人質疑，在6月及7月均未升息後，聯準會這次是否真會行動；道明證券仍以維持利率為基本情境。

就業基準修正初值也說明決策為何不容易。3月非農就業人數預計下修7.9萬、約0.1%，市場原本預期上修18.3萬。調整前，未經季節調整的就業人數在截至3月的一年增加21.1萬，平均每月約1.76萬；修正後平均增幅將降至約1.1萬。總修正幅度遠小於前次年度下調的91.1萬，也低於過去十年平均絕對調整幅度0.2%。

民間部門比總數更弱。私人就業下修17.8萬，其中製造業減6.7萬，貿易、運輸及公用事業減9.8萬，政府就業則上修9.9萬。這不是強勁的聘僱趨勢，但也不像前次基準修正，需要對整個就業市場重新作大幅判斷。

芝加哥PMI從57.6驟降至47.1，遠低於預估的58.3。密西根信心終值51.7，雖優於預估51.0，仍低於7月的55.2。一年期通膨預期由初值4.2%下修至4.0%，低於預估4.3%；五年期維持3.3%。活動與信心轉弱，家庭較長期的物價預期卻仍偏高。

Warsh希望市場依經濟基本面，而非央行談話交易；但他上任後最大的三次單日曲線變動，都發生在公開露面之後。週五再次顯示，投資人仍高度依賴他如何描述緊縮程度，以及能接受多快的通膨下降。這次談話釐清了目標與工具，卻沒有界定下一次行動的門檻。

## 日本大舉護匯，短債標售需求卻轉弱

日本公布7月30日至8月26日共動用創紀錄的¥15.4兆、約$964億干預，今年累計約¥27兆。操作曾使日圓從每美元近164升至最強155.23，美國也在7月31日加入，為1998年以來首次聯手支撐日圓。但到週五東京晚間，匯價已回到約159.68。干預改變了部位，仍未消除利差、進口石油成本及財政疑慮。

東京通膨增加日本央行行動的理由。8月扣除生鮮食品物價年增1.8%，高於前期1.7%，符合預期；再扣除能源後達2.0%，服務價格上漲1.4%。租金、餐飲、醫療費用與耐久財均有貢獻，失業率僅2.4%，每名求職者對應1.18個職缺。補貼與基期效果抵銷部分壓力：能源價格下降2.0%，汽油跌2.7%，電價跌2.4%，米價則在前一年急升後回落14.2%。

2年期日債標售投標倍數降至2.97，低於前次3.63及過去12個月平均3.74；標售尾差由0.007擴大至0.034，為2016年以來最大，期貨維持下跌。2年期殖利率已從8月初約1.56%升至1.70%，10年期達2.92%。交換市場反映9月升息機率約82%至84%。

各部會預算需求可能超過創紀錄的¥130兆，對照本年度初始與追加預算合計約¥125兆。擬議食品消費稅減免將使收入減少約¥5兆，稅收降至約¥83兆，加上約¥9兆非稅收入，資金缺口仍接近¥40兆。高市早苗希望新增發債低於¥40兆，本年度各項預算合計則為¥32.7兆；但這仍是目標，尚非財源已落實的支出計畫。

企業混合資本債仍找到買方。截至9月發行額可望約¥1.18兆，為2021會計年度以來最多。Panasonic發行¥1,000億次順位債，其中六年一個月後可贖回券，對日債利差110個基點、票息3.455%；十年一個月後可贖回券，利差130個基點、票息4.188%。住友林業計畫發行約¥2,500億、35至40年期次順位債，置換收購過橋貸款。日本另有約¥1.32兆混合資本債在2026會計年度進入首次贖回日，增加再融資需求。

墨西哥也在日圓市場發行長債，兩年來首次武士債募集¥2,828億，接近2024年8月¥1,522億的兩倍。四個券期從3.5年至20年，定價為日圓交換利率加115至210個基點。這顯示墨西哥仍可取得日本資金，不等於其財政及Pemex相關信評壓力已改善。

## 歐洲通膨加快，法國財政辯論增添不確定性

西班牙8月通膨升至4.5%，為2023年以來最快；法國加速至2.7%，創5月以來高點並超過預估，兩者主要都受能源推動。歐元區整體預估由2.9%升至3.3%，核心則仍估2.5%。

斯洛維尼亞央行總裁Primoz Dolenc認為，通膨沒有自行消退，理由偏向支持歐洲央行9月升息，12月預測再提供重新評估中期路徑的機會。拉脫維亞的Martins Kazaks表示，再升息有相當可能，並警告物價高增長持續的風險。奧地利的Martin Kocher指出，第2季成長0.4%反映動能比一般認知更強，但也承認明確的工資及其他第二輪效應尚未出現。市場普遍預期存款利率再升25個基點至2.5%。

英國央行總裁Bailey更重視就業偏弱、職缺減少及民間薪資增速放緩。他認為第二輪效應仍溫和，可以先觀察能源衝擊；7月他也加入6比3維持利率的多數。不過，市場仍完全反映今年一次、明年春季前再一次各25個基點的升息，家庭一年期通膨預期則達3.9%。

法國首場總統辯論擴大了財政前景的分歧。Jean-Luc Mélenchon主張協商取消歐洲央行持有的法國債務，表示現階段並未針對私人債權人。Marine Le Pen宣稱可藉縮小政府、減少移民及可能削減歐盟分攤款，節省€1,250億，卻仍保留可能讓民眾60歲退休、每年成本約€90億的年金主張。Edouard Philippe警告，拒付債務風險可能使法國失去融資管道。

10年期法德利差接近85個基點，高於2026年初不到60個基點。修正後GDP顯示第1季萎縮0.2%、第2季零成長。能源價格上升時，法國幾乎沒有成長動能可以抵銷更高的債務成本。

美國收盤後，惠譽維持法國A+、展望穩定，距投機級還有六個級距。評級機構預估2026、2027及2028年赤字分別占GDP 5.2%、5.5%及5.2%，並警告財政整頓若不足，可能先轉負向展望，再面臨降評壓力。這次確認提供喘息，但沒有解決財政惡化。

能源消息在週五收盤後繼續發展。當日布蘭特小跌0.43%至$89.31，WTI跌0.16%至$83.40；週日美國對伊朗火箭發射器發動數週來首次攻擊，隨後亞洲早盤布蘭特上漲1.9%至$89.75。這是下一個交易時段的新變化，不是週五盤勢的原因。另外，一項安排預計讓美國取得委內瑞拉逾650億桶已探明儲量的多數控制權，委內瑞拉每桶可保留$19利潤。這種較長期的控制權變化，尚不能立即緩解伊朗情勢升級。

## AI融資擴及銀行貸款、設備債務與可轉債

軟銀正尋求$100億、兩年期貸款，利率約為SOFR加275個基點，由瑞穗擔任主辦行及簿記管理人，可用於償還部分$400億OpenAI過橋貸款。這筆新案增加短期銀行融資選項，與先前可能發行至多$200億債券、以及以OpenAI持股擔保的$100億融資並行；後者可能要求補繳現金擔保或提前還款。到10月，軟銀須完成接近$650億的OpenAI投資。

Lambda透過摩根大通安排約$10億短期私募債，購買Nvidia GPU出租給微軟；8月稍早另完成$9.26億GPU與基礎設施貸款。客戶租約有助確認設備需求，但期限短，設備表現與再融資仍重要。Lambda同時也討論募集至多$30億股本。

Iren取得Blue Owl基金領投的$24億方案，包括$12億優先擔保定期貸款及$12億優先擔保票據，兩者均支付9%，在撥款後兩年半到期，Pimco也參與。分階段動用資金將購買Nvidia Blackwell Ultra GPU，供加拿大園區使用；公司預估2027會計年度資本支出至多$300億，財報後股價下跌近13%。債權人雖有擔保品保障，融資卻會在整體投資計畫完全展開前到期。

全球可轉債發行達$1,470億，比2025年同期快逾50%，並已超過2021年全年紀錄。市場平均delta約64%，接近上一波熱潮以來高點，部分新券票息則近零。Nebius在先前$97.5億發行後再募集$45億，部分2030年券票息區間僅0%至0.5%。買方接受極低利息以參與股價上漲，下檔卻仍承擔無擔保債權風險。

Pimco認為AI發債速度過快、數量過多，市場消化不良可能是8月稍早10年期美債殖利率接近4.75%的原因之一。這是該公司的評估，並非已確認的殖利率變動歸因。週五實質殖利率上升、半導體下跌3.48%，顯示股權與融資對利率有共同敏感度；但對個別債權回收而言，新貸款的擔保品及期限，比單一產業標籤更重要。

報告涵蓋期間稍後，台灣公布對主要海外買方有影響的漸進調整。金管會主委彭金隆要求壽險業降低支應台幣負債的外國資產、增加國內投資；若持續買入美元資產，則應多銷售美元保單。壽險業管理資產超過$1.2兆，海外部位逾$6,900億，其中約$1,620億為美國公司債。

年度幣別錯配目標已納入高階主管績效評估。惠譽估計，未來五至七年海外配置可能下降數個百分點，降至略高於60%到約65%。台灣希望三年內吸引NT$3,000億壽險資金回流，但國內適合標的不足，限制調整速度。這不是強制賣出；不過，美國科技與基建發債增加時，如此大型買方降低再投資，也可能影響需求。

## 優質借款人找到替代管道，弱勢信用面對現金流限制

瑞銀首次在中國境內發債，募集CN¥20億，5年期熊貓債票息1.78%，為同年期外國金融發行人最低票息、最窄境內基準利差。2026年熊貓債發行創紀錄達CN¥2,140億，年增67%，平均票息比美元發債低約200個基點。中國低利率吸引海外借款人，資本管制卻仍限制市場規模。

印度企業因短端重新定價而調整期限。Power Finance撤回較短券期，改以7.55%發行15年債；REC取消原訂2年券，繼續推進約10年期融資；Bajaj Finance則發行₹500億10年債，由印度人壽保險公司全數買下。8月3年期殖利率升32個基點，10年期升22個基點，一度使最高評級10年借款比3年便宜。市場預期印度央行只進行50至75個基點的短週期升息，長端又有退休基金與公積金穩定需求。Vedanta則在3月發行₹757.5億後，仍計畫以至少₹100億、3至7年期債再融資。

南非希望最快本會計年度發行首檔主權綠色債券，須視10月中期預算及市場情況而定。金額與幣別未定，本幣、歐元及美元皆可能。當局估計2026至2035年氣候計畫執行與減緩需求達R3.7兆，並希望到2030年每年從國際氣候融資機構取得約R1,600億。能源、輸電、水務、住宅及勞工轉型專案，正依永續融資架構確認資格。

Acrisure的$44億2030年貸款下跌10%至約83美分，成為彭博美國槓桿貸款指數8月最大拖累；$11億2030年高收益債最低約87美分，也成為相應公司債指數第二大負面貢獻。市場追查Guggenheim先前參與優先股融資的少數部位，加劇賣壓，但關係比空頭暗示的有限。

營運數字本身已有足夠疑慮：第2季EBITDA減少約12%至$3.45億，內生成長下滑0.6%；標普計算含優先股槓桿為15.4倍，排除後仍9.6倍。約$8億加回項目占$16億調整後EBITDA的一半，因此預定$3億節流，對降槓桿計畫格外重要。

雪梨開發商Bathla在興建數千戶較平價公寓時進入破產程序，負債約A$33億。約40家私人貸款機構提供資金，PAG、CVS Lane及Centuria Bass合計超過A$10億，其中PAG逾A$3億。顧問正尋求新資本維持專案運作，但融資及建築成本高、房價偏弱，又有房產投資人稅制變動。債權人協調與未完工專案估值，將決定回收情況。

穆迪將塞內加爾由Caa1降至Caa2、展望負向，理由是流動性壓力急迫，違約或債務處理的可能性提高。2025年底中央政府債務接近GDP 117%，廣義公共債務逾130%，2026年融資需求約26%。國際貨幣基金在發現$70億未揭露債務後，暫停$18億計畫。總統Bassirou Diomaye Faye與前總理Ousmane Sonko決裂，後者目前擔任由其政黨控制的國會議長，使重整及改革更難協調。在新IMF架構尚未建立前，依賴區域市場使轉貸壓力維持高檔。

巴西7月正式就業增加58,568人，低於預估11.5萬，也是2026年最低單月增幅。個人貸款違約率由7.4%升至7.8%，創2009年以來高點；企業由4.0%升至4.2%。總放款仍增加0.3%至R$7.4兆，但個人貸款平均利率60%，信用卡循環利率達436.2%。政府因車貸方案申請不佳，將最長還款期從72個月延至84個月。央行警告，即使Selic仍在14%、家庭已高度負債，更多刺激仍可能支撐需求及通膨。

Shapoorji Pallonji正討論變現其18.4% Tata Sons股權，包括換成上市Tata公司股票、由海外銀行融資直接買回，或售予外部投資人。結構與估值均未定，監管障礙也仍在。Eqyizen Investment債券支付18.95%，期限36個月，首次付息在2028年7月。若達成協議，可提供還債流動性並減輕Tata Sons上市壓力；否則，債權人仍依賴這筆缺乏流動性的策略持股變現。

## 就業與CPI將檢驗短端重新定價

職缺及ISM製造業、服務業將顯示芝加哥的疲弱是否擴散，以及投入價格是否仍堅挺。8月非農預估增加5.5萬人、失業率4.1%；9月11日公布8月CPI，之後是9月15至16日聯準會會議。若就業弱、物價也降溫，將挑戰週五短端大幅上升的幅度；通膨若持續，則支持市場從Warsh談話聽出的急迫性。

9月10日歐洲央行決策前，德國通膨預估3.1%，歐元區整體3.3%、核心2.5%。若只有能源推高整體、核心持穩，9月後是否續升仍有討論空間；服務或工資壓力若擴散，較長緊縮路徑的理由就更強。週日軍事升級，是這些數據以外新增的風險。

軟銀銀行承諾截止日為8月31日；Bathla首次債權人會議在9月4日，將討論維持專案運作及約40家貸款機構間的協調。日本預算需求與後續短券標售，則將在央行可能升息前，繼續提供供需狀況的線索。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
## Warsh sends short yields higher despite weaker economic readings

Treasuries fell sharply at the front end after Kevin Warsh said inflation progress was inadequate and financial conditions were difficult to describe as restrictive. He made no commitment to a September increase, but investors raised the probability of one. Two-year yields jumped 14 basis points to 4.34%, their biggest increase in more than two months. Five-year yields rose 10 basis points to 4.48%, the 10-year added 6 to 4.73%, and the 30-year rose 3 to 5.22%.

The curve flattened rather than repeating the long-end selloff that followed Warsh's July press conference. Two-to-10-year spreads narrowed 8 basis points to 39, and 2s30s narrowed 11 to 88. Ten-year real yields climbed 8 basis points to 2.42% while breakevens fell 2 to 2.31%. A 0.52% dollar gain and 2.85% decline in gold accompanied the higher expected real-rate path.

The chair's message outweighed softer data released the same morning. Chicago PMI fell into contraction, the preliminary payroll benchmark reduced employment rather than increasing it as expected, and Michigan sentiment remained below July's level. Those readings left a September decision open even as markets inferred more urgency from Warsh's commitment to the 2% target.

Semiconductors fell 3.48%, the Nasdaq 100 lost 0.71% and the S&P 500 declined 0.27%, although VIX edged down to 14.42. Broad bond funds recorded modest losses. Long Treasuries briefly rallied during the speech before closing lower; the 30-year yield remained 13 basis points above a month earlier. A flatter curve showed a greater expected policy response, not the disappearance of supply and financing pressures. Japan's weak short-bond auction and a new round of AI borrowing provided separate reminders of those demands.

## A firm inflation target, but no promised September decision

Warsh called the 2% PCE objective firm and fixed. Better summer readings had not yet meaningfully improved the underlying inflation trend, he said, and progress needed to be clear and sufficiently fast. He identified short-term interest rates as the Fed's predominant tool while questioning whether broad financial conditions were restrictive. Investors heard a stronger case for conventional tightening even without explicit forward guidance.

Federal funds futures initially lifted September hike odds above 50% from about 36% before the address; later swaps pricing reached roughly 60%. Barclays changed its forecast to 25-basis-point increases in September and December. Not everyone followed. Investors at ABN AMRO and Brandywine questioned whether the Fed would act after holding in June and July, and TD Securities retained a hold as its base case.

The preliminary payroll benchmark showed why the decision remained difficult. March nonfarm employment is set to be revised down 79,000, or 0.1%, against expectations of a 183,000 increase. Before revision, non-seasonally adjusted payrolls had grown by 211,000 over the year through March, about 17,600 a month; the adjustment would reduce that average to roughly 11,000. The total revision was much smaller than the prior annual reduction of 911,000 and below the preceding decade's average absolute adjustment of 0.2%.

Private employment was weaker than the aggregate suggested. It was marked down 178,000, including 67,000 in manufacturing and 98,000 in trade, transportation and utilities, while government employment was revised up 99,000. The figures did not show a vigorous hiring trend, but neither did they force the wholesale reassessment that the previous benchmark had prompted.

Chicago PMI dropped to 47.1 from 57.6, far below the 58.3 forecast. Final Michigan sentiment reached 51.7, above the 51.0 estimate but down from 55.2 in July. One-year inflation expectations were revised to 4.0% from the preliminary 4.2%, below the 4.3% consensus; five-year expectations held at 3.3%. Activity and confidence were weakening, while longer-run household price expectations remained elevated.

Warsh wants markets to respond to fundamentals rather than central-bank commentary, yet the three largest daily curve changes since his appointment have followed his appearances. Friday's response illustrated how much information investors still extract from his descriptions of restraint and the acceptable speed of disinflation. The target and policy tool were clearer after the speech; the threshold for the next move was not.

## Japan spends heavily on yen support as auction demand weakens

Japan disclosed record intervention of ¥15.4 trillion, or $96.4 billion, between July 30 and August 26, taking this year's total to about ¥27 trillion. The campaign moved the yen from almost 164 per dollar to a strongest level of 155.23, with the US joining on July 31 in the first coordinated yen support since 1998. By Friday evening in Tokyo it was back near 159.68. Intervention had changed positioning without removing rate differentials, oil-import costs or fiscal concerns.

Tokyo inflation reinforced expectations that the BOJ would also act. August prices excluding fresh food rose 1.8%, up from 1.7% and matching consensus. Excluding fresh food and energy, inflation reached 2.0%; services rose 1.4%. Rents, restaurants, medical fees and durable goods contributed, with unemployment at 2.4% and 1.18 jobs per applicant. Subsidies and comparison effects offset some of that pressure: energy prices fell 2.0%, gasoline 2.7%, electricity 2.4% and rice 14.2% after the prior year's surge.

The 2-year JGB auction drew a bid-to-cover ratio of 2.97, down from 3.63 at the previous sale and a 12-month average of 3.74. Its tail widened to 0.034 from 0.007, the largest since 2016, and futures stayed lower. Two-year yields had already climbed to 1.70% from about 1.56% at the start of August; the 10-year reached 2.92%. Swaps assigned roughly 82%–84% odds to a September hike.

Budget requests could exceed a record ¥130 trillion, compared with about ¥125 trillion across the current initial and supplementary plans. A proposed food consumption-tax cut would reduce receipts by around ¥5 trillion, leaving tax revenue near ¥83 trillion. Another ¥9 trillion of non-tax revenue would still leave a gap close to ¥40 trillion. Sanae Takaichi wants new bond issuance below ¥40 trillion, versus ¥32.7 trillion across the current budgets, but that intention is not yet a funded spending plan.

Corporate hybrids nevertheless found demand. Issuance is on course for roughly ¥1.18 trillion through September, the most since fiscal 2021. Panasonic sold ¥100 billion of subordinated bonds: the tranche callable after six years and one month priced at 110 basis points over JGBs with a 3.455% coupon; the ten-year-and-one-month call tranche priced at 130 basis points and 4.188%. Sumitomo Forestry plans about ¥250 billion of 35- to 40-year subordinated debt to refinance an acquisition bridge. Around ¥1.32 trillion of Japanese hybrids reach first call dates in fiscal 2026, adding to refinancing demand.

Mexico also placed long yen debt, raising ¥282.8 billion in its first Samurai sale in two years, nearly twice August 2024's ¥152.2 billion. Four tranches from 3.5 to 20 years priced 115–210 basis points over yen swaps. That demonstrated access to Japanese buyers despite Mexico's fiscal and Pemex-related rating pressures, not an improvement in those risks by itself.

## European inflation accelerates while France's fiscal debate widens

Spanish August inflation rose to 4.5%, its fastest since 2023, and French inflation accelerated to 2.7%, the highest since May and above forecasts. Energy drove both increases. The euro-area aggregate was expected at 3.3%, up from 2.9%, with core inflation still forecast at 2.5%.

Slovenia's Primoz Dolenc said the arguments favored a September ECB increase because inflation was not resolving itself, with December projections offering the next opportunity to reassess the medium-term path. Latvia's Martins Kazaks called another hike a considerable possibility and warned against persistent elevated inflation. Austria's Martin Kocher pointed to stronger-than-perceived momentum after 0.4% Q2 growth, while acknowledging that clear wage and other second-round effects had not yet appeared. Markets widely expected 25 basis points to take the deposit rate to 2.5%.

Andrew Bailey put more weight on weak UK employment, falling vacancies and slower private-sector wage growth. Second-round effects remained subdued, the BOE governor said, supporting time to observe the energy shock. He had joined July's 6–3 majority for a hold. Markets nonetheless fully priced one 25-basis-point increase this year and another by spring, while one-year household inflation expectations reached 3.9%.

France's first presidential debate added fiscal uncertainty. Jean-Luc Mélenchon advocated negotiating cancellation of debt held by the ECB, saying private creditors were not his target at this stage. Marine Le Pen claimed €125 billion of savings from a smaller state, reduced immigration and possible EU contribution cuts, while retaining a pension proposal that could allow retirement at 60 and cost about €9 billion annually. Edouard Philippe warned that repudiation risk could close France's access to finance.

The 10-year spread over Germany was near 85 basis points, compared with less than 60 at the start of 2026. Revised GDP showed a 0.2% Q1 contraction and no Q2 growth. Rising energy prices therefore arrived in an economy with little growth to offset higher debt-service costs.

After the US close, Fitch affirmed France at A+ with a stable outlook, six notches above speculative grade. It projected deficits of 5.2% of GDP in 2026, 5.5% in 2027 and 5.2% in 2028, and warned that insufficient consolidation could lead first to a negative outlook and then rating pressure. The affirmation offered a reprieve without resolving the fiscal deterioration.

Energy developments also continued after Friday's modest oil decline—Brent closed down 0.43% at $89.31 and WTI down 0.16% at $83.40. On Sunday, the US struck Iranian rocket launchers in its first attack in weeks; Brent subsequently rose 1.9% to $89.75 in early Asian trading. That was a new development for the next session, not a cause of Friday's close. Separately, an arrangement was expected to give the US majority control over more than 65 billion barrels of Venezuelan proven reserves while leaving Venezuela $19 profit per barrel. That longer-term change in control did not provide immediate relief from the Iranian escalation.

## AI borrowing expands through bank loans, equipment debt and convertibles

SoftBank is seeking a $10 billion, two-year loan at about 275 basis points over SOFR, with Mizuho as mandated lead arranger and bookrunner. It could repay part of the $40 billion OpenAI bridge loan. The new request adds a short-dated bank option alongside the already-reported possible bond sale of up to $20 billion and the $10 billion facility secured by its OpenAI stake, which can require additional cash collateral or early repayment. Nearly $65 billion of OpenAI investment is due by October.

Lambda raised about $1 billion of short-term private debt arranged by JPMorgan to buy Nvidia GPUs for lease to Microsoft, following a separate $926 million August loan for GPUs and infrastructure. The customer lease helps establish equipment demand, but short maturities leave performance and refinancing important. Lambda is also discussing up to $3 billion of equity funding.

Iren secured a $2.4 billion package led by Blue Owl funds: a $1.2 billion senior-secured term loan and $1.2 billion of senior-secured notes, each paying 9% and maturing two-and-a-half years after funding. Pimco participated. Staged draws fund Nvidia Blackwell Ultra GPUs for a Canadian campus, while Iren forecasts as much as $30 billion of fiscal 2027 capital spending. Its shares fell almost 13% after earnings. The financing provides collateral protection, but matures well before the broader investment program has fully played out.

Global convertible issuance reached $147 billion, more than 50% ahead of the comparable 2025 period and already above 2021's full-year record. Average delta was roughly 64%, around the highest since that boom, while some new coupons approached zero. Nebius raised $4.5 billion after $9.75 billion of earlier issuance; part of the new 2030 debt carried a 0%–0.5% coupon range. Buyers were accepting little income in exchange for equity participation while retaining unsecured downside exposure.

Pimco described AI issuance as too much, too fast, and suggested indigestion may have contributed to the 10-year Treasury yield approaching 4.75% earlier in August. That remains its assessment rather than an attribution of the yield move. Friday's 3.48% semiconductor decline as real yields rose illustrated the shared sensitivity across equity and financing, but the new loans' collateral and maturities matter more to individual recoveries than a single sector label.

Later in the reporting window, Taiwan disclosed a gradual change affecting a major overseas buyer. Financial regulator Peng Jin-lung is directing life insurers to reduce foreign assets backing Taiwan-dollar liabilities, invest more domestically and sell more dollar policies when buying dollar assets. Insurers manage over $1.2 trillion, hold more than $690 billion overseas and own about $162 billion of US corporate bonds.

Annual currency-mismatch targets now affect senior executives' assessments. Fitch estimated foreign allocations could fall several percentage points toward the mid- or low-60% range over five to seven years. Taiwan aims to attract NT$300 billion of insurer capital home over three years, although limited domestic assets constrain the pace. This is not forced liquidation, but slower reinvestment by such a large buyer could matter alongside heavier US technology and infrastructure issuance.

## Strong borrowers find alternatives; weaker credits confront cash-flow limits

UBS raised 2 billion yuan in its first domestic Chinese bond, a 5-year panda at 1.78%, the lowest coupon and tightest onshore benchmark spread for a foreign financial issuer of that maturity. Panda issuance reached a record 214 billion yuan in 2026, up 67% year over year; average coupons were about 200 basis points below dollar issuance. Low Chinese rates attracted foreign borrowers, although capital controls still limited the market's scale.

Indian companies shifted maturities as the short end repriced. Power Finance withdrew a shorter sale but issued 15-year debt at 7.55%. REC canceled a planned 2-year note while proceeding around ten years, and Bajaj Finance sold 50 billion rupees of 10-year debt entirely to Life Insurance Corp. Three-year yields rose 32 basis points in August versus 22 at ten years, briefly making top-rated 10-year borrowing cheaper than 3-year debt. Expectations of a short 50–75-basis-point RBI cycle met steady pension and provident-fund demand for long maturities. Vedanta still planned at least 10 billion rupees of 3- to 7-year refinancing after issuing 75.75 billion in March.

South Africa aims to issue its first sovereign green bond as early as the current fiscal year, subject to October's medium-term budget and market conditions. Amount and currency remain open—domestic, euro and dollar markets are possible. Authorities estimate 3.7 trillion rand of climate implementation and mitigation needs for 2026–2035 and seek around 160 billion annually from international climate-finance institutions by 2030. Eligible energy, transmission, water, housing and worker-transition projects are being identified under a sustainable-finance framework.

Acrisure's $4.4 billion loan due 2030 fell 10% to around 83 cents, making it the Bloomberg US Leveraged Loan Index's largest August detractor. Its $1.1 billion of 2030 high-yield bonds traded as low as about 87 and were the second-largest drag on the corresponding corporate index. Scrutiny of Guggenheim's minority role in earlier preferred-equity financings intensified the selloff, although the connection was narrower than short sellers implied.

Operating figures provided substantial reasons for concern: Q2 EBITDA fell about 12% to $345 million, organic growth declined 0.6%, and S&P calculated leverage at 15.4 times including preferred equity or 9.6 times excluding it. Around $800 million of addbacks represented half of $1.6 billion adjusted EBITDA. A planned $300 million cost reduction was therefore important to the deleveraging case.

Sydney developer Bathla entered insolvency with about A$3.3 billion of debt while building thousands of lower-cost apartments. Roughly 40 private lenders financed it. PAG, CVS Lane and Centuria Bass together extended more than A$1 billion, including over A$300 million from PAG. The adviser is seeking new capital to keep projects operating amid high financing and construction costs, weak home prices and property-investor tax changes. Creditor coordination and unfinished-project valuations will shape recoveries.

Moody's cut Senegal to Caa2 from Caa1 with a negative outlook, citing acute liquidity risk and a greater likelihood of default or debt treatment. Central-government debt was near 117% of GDP at end-2025, broader public debt above 130%, and 2026 financing needs around 26%. The IMF suspended its $1.8 billion program after discovery of $7 billion in undisclosed debt. President Bassirou Diomaye Faye's break with former premier Ousmane Sonko—now speaker of a parliament controlled by his party—complicates restructuring and reform. Reliance on regional markets leaves rollover pressure high while a new IMF framework remains absent.

Brazil's formal job creation slowed to 58,568 in July, versus a 115,000 forecast and the weakest monthly result of 2026. Personal-loan defaults rose to 7.8% from 7.4%, their highest since 2009; corporate defaults increased to 4.2% from 4.0%. Lending still grew 0.3% to 7.4 trillion reais, but average personal-loan rates reached 60% and revolving credit-card rates 436.2%. The government extended a poorly subscribed vehicle-financing program's maximum repayment period to 84 months from 72. The central bank warned that more stimulus could sustain demand and inflation, even with Selic at 14% and households already heavily indebted.

Shapoorji Pallonji is discussing ways to monetize its 18.4% Tata Sons stake: a swap into listed Tata-company shares, a direct buyout financed by overseas banks, or an outside sale. No structure or valuation is agreed, and regulatory obstacles remain. Eqyizen Investment bonds pay 18.95%, mature in 36 months and first pay interest in July 2028. A settlement could provide repayment liquidity and ease pressure for a Tata Sons listing; absent one, creditors remain dependent on realizing an illiquid strategic holding.

## Jobs and CPI will test the front-end repricing

Job openings and ISM manufacturing and services will show whether Chicago's weakness extends further and whether input prices remain firm. August payroll expectations center on 55,000 jobs and 4.1% unemployment. August CPI on September 11 then precedes the September 15–16 Fed meeting. Weak employment combined with softer prices would challenge Friday's sharp short-end move; persistent inflation would support the urgency investors heard in Warsh's speech.

Germany's inflation forecast is 3.1%, with the euro area at 3.3% headline and 2.5% core ahead of the September 10 ECB decision. Energy-led acceleration with stable core would leave room to debate hikes beyond September; broader services or wage pressure would strengthen the case for a longer response. The Sunday military escalation is a new risk around those releases.

SoftBank bank commitments are due August 31. Bathla's first creditor meeting on September 4 will address support for ongoing projects and coordination among about 40 lenders. Japanese budget requests and subsequent short-maturity auctions will provide further evidence on supply and demand as a BOJ increase approaches.

overall_summary.headline: Short Treasuries sell off as Warsh demands faster inflation progress
overall_summary.session_narrative:
Warsh called 2% inflation a fixed objective and questioned whether financial conditions were restrictive. September hike odds rose above 50%, later reaching about 60% in swaps. The curve bear-flattened: 2s30s narrowed 11 basis points to 88, while the 30-year still closed higher at 5.22%.

The employment benchmark cut March payrolls by 79,000 rather than the expected increase. Chicago PMI fell to 47.1 and Michigan sentiment remained below July. Those releases kept the actual September decision open even as policy expectations moved higher.

Japan disclosed record yen intervention and a weak 2-year auction. European inflation accelerated, while AI borrowers added short loans, secured equipment debt and convertibles. France's later rating affirmation and Sunday's Iran strike were post-close developments, not causes of Friday's Treasury move.
overall_summary.summary: Two-year yields jumped 14 basis points to 4.34%, while the 10-year rose 6 to 4.73%. Higher real yields and lower breakevens accompanied Warsh's firm inflation message, despite weaker hiring and survey readings.
